html:
Khoomei, or throat singing, is a way of singing in western Mongolia and nearby Tuva in which one singer makes two or more notes at once: a low drone and a high whistling melody above it.

It grew among herders of the Altai mountains, said to imitate the sounds of wind, water and animals. Its age is not known; it was long passed on within families, and is often sung with the horsehead fiddle, the morin khuur. Under socialism it was taught in state ensembles, and from the 1990s it became known abroad.

UNESCO listed Mongolian khoomei as world heritage in 2010. Rock bands such as The Hu mix it with heavy metal, and it is part of the nomad image that Mongolia presents to the world, with Naadam and the eagle hunters.
sum: Khoomei, or throat singing, is a way of singing in western Mongolia and nearby Tuva in which one singer makes two or more notes at once: a low drone and a high whistling melody above it.
